unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 6: LIFE IN THE WORLD & CULTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students prepare a project titled "Global Food Culture and Preferences", focusing on the themes of continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; and food culture from different parts of the world. First, they research continents, countries, and nationalities, describing their unique features. Then, they explore how people shop for food, talk about personal preferences like vegan, halal, or gluten-free, and highlight traditional and modern dishes. Finally, they look at foods from different cultures, such as sushi, baklava, and pizza, and discuss healthy and unhealthy eating habits. They should use creative elements such as maps, charts, or videos and present their projects in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the world and culture with its components such as continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student of an upper secondary school in year 10 may know what life in the world and culture, continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an an upper secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the world and culture'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''Healthy Food: vegetable, fruit, beans, a carrot, garlic, grapes, mushroom, onion, rice, grilled, boiled; Unhealthy Food: a burger, biscuit (cookie-US), cereal, fast food, chips (French fries-US); countries such as France, Germany and so on'' and also some structures such as ''How long have you been shopping for traditional dishes? She has lived in Italy since 2020, and she loves Italian pasta. I have some bananas in the fridge. They have already tried sushi in Japan. We have just bought some fresh vegetables from the supermarket.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about international foods, their countries of origin, and types through collaborative discussion and critical thinking by using the target vocabulary. Activity : Food Detective Challenge The teacher explains that students play a game as ''Food Detectives'' to solve a mystery about three international dishes. The teacher plays an audio or reads a script with clues about the foods, such as their country of origin, type (e.g., dessert, main course), and cultural significance. Students listen carefully and fill out a worksheet with the following details: Food Name: Country of Origin: Type of Dish (Dessert/Main Course/Snack): Next, they work in groups to compare answers. Then, each group creates a new clue for a different food and exchanges it with another group to solve. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about popular international food items and their countries of origin in English by using target vocabulary. Activity : Exploring Food Cultures Around the World The teacher begins the lesson by showing students pictures of popular international foods (e.g., pizza, sushi, baklava, tacos, croissants) and asking if they know where these foods come from or if they have tried them. The teacher provides a list of foods and their countries of origin, then writes example sentences on the board, such as ''Pizza is from Italy'', or ''Baklava is a traditional Turkish dessert''. Students write their own sentences following this structure. Each student then chooses a favourite food from another culture, draws it, and labels it with a sentence such as ''Tacos are from Mexico''. Finally, students present their drawings to the class, explaining what the food is, where it is from, and why they like it. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
